# trace: `TraceSlice`

The `data` payload of `openreadout trace FILE --json`, inside the [envelope](envelope.md).

Output of `trace`: a window of one sweep of one trace.

JSON Schema: [`docs/schema/trace.schema.json`](https://github.com/openreadout/openreadout/blob/main/docs/schema/trace.schema.json) · also printed by `openreadout self schema trace`.

## Fields

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | The input file. |
| `format` | `string` | yes | Format id of the input file. |
| `trace` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Trace index (see `info` → `traces[]`). |
| `sweep` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Sweep index. |
| `sweep_count` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Sweeps in the trace. |
| `sample_rate_hz` | `number` (double) | yes | Samples per second. |
| `sweep_sample_count` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Samples in this sweep. |
| `first_sample` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | First sample of the window (zero-based, within the sweep). |
| `sample_count` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Samples in the window (statistics cover all of them). |
| `start_s` | `number` (double) | yes | Time of the first window sample in seconds. Single-sweep traces use the trace's own clock: `info.traces[].start_s + first_sample / sample_rate_hz` (a chromatogram's retention time, negative when acquisition began before injection; an electrophysiology recording's clock). Multi-sweep traces are timed from the start of the sweep (`first_sample / sample_rate_hz`; `sweep_start_s` places the sweep in the recording). Irregularly sampled traces (`sample_rate_hz` 0 with a `time` channel) report that channel's first window value; traces without a time base (spectra) report 0. |
| `sweep_start_s` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Time of the sweep's first sample on the recording clock, seconds, when the file records it (`info.traces[].start_s` for a single sweep, `extra.sweep_starts_s[sweep]` for multi-sweep traces). |
| `channels` | array of [`TraceChannelSlice`](#tracechannelslice) | yes | One entry per requested channel. |
| `truncated` | `boolean` | yes | True when fewer samples are returned than the window holds. |
| `axis` | any JSON |  | The trace's abscissa (`info` → `traces[].extra.axis`: `{quantity, unit, first, step, …}`), e.g. the ppm axis of an NMR spectrum or a chromatogram's retention time in minutes; sample `i` of the sweep is at `first + i * step`. For a time axis this agrees with `start_s` and `sample_rate_hz` (`first` = `start_s` at `first_sample` 0, `step` = 1 / `sample_rate_hz`, in `unit`). Irregular axes (`irregular: true`) name the channel holding each sample's abscissa instead. |
| `x_range` | array of 2 × `number` (double) or `null` |  | The axis window asked for (`x_range`, low to high): axis units, or seconds for signals without an axis. `first_sample`/`sample_count` are the samples inside it. |

## Types

### TraceChannelSlice

One channel of a `TraceSlice`.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Channel index. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | Channel name. |
| `unit` | `string` or `null` |  | Physical unit of the samples. |
| `stats` | [`TraceStats`](#tracestats) | yes | Statistics over the whole window. |
| `samples` | array of `number` (double) | yes | The first `max_samples` samples of the window, scaled to `unit`. |

### TraceStats

Summary statistics of one channel over the requested window.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Samples in the window. |
| `finite` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Finite samples (NaN/inf are skipped by min/max/mean/std). |
| `min` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Smallest finite sample. |
| `max` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Largest finite sample. |
| `mean` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Mean of the finite samples. |
| `std` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Population standard deviation. |
| `argmin` | `integer` (uint64) or `null` |  | Sample index of the minimum, counted from the start of the sweep (not of the window: the index within `samples` is `argmin - first_sample`). |
| `argmax` | `integer` (uint64) or `null` |  | Sample index of the maximum, counted from the start of the sweep (not of the window: the index within `samples` is `argmax - first_sample`). |
| `argmin_time_s` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Time of the minimum in seconds, on the same clock as the slice's `start_s`. Absent when the trace has no time base (a spectrum; see `argmin_axis_value`). |
| `argmax_time_s` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Time of the maximum in seconds, on the same clock as the slice's `start_s` (for a chromatogram: the retention time of the tallest point, in seconds). |
| `argmin_axis_value` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Position of the minimum on the slice's `axis`, in `axis.unit` (retention time in minutes, chemical shift in ppm, wavenumber, …). Present only when the slice has an `axis`. |
| `argmax_axis_value` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Position of the maximum on the slice's `axis`, in `axis.unit`: `axis.first + argmax * axis.step`, or the abscissa channel's value for an irregular axis. |
